sections.name: What Actually Causes Brain Freeze
lines: Drink a slushie too fast, and you get this. Brain freeze.
But your brain isn't freezing. It can't even feel pain itself.
The cold hits the roof of your mouth, right below some important blood vessels.
They suddenly tighten, then quickly widen again, to warm things back up.
That sudden rush is picked up by a big nerve in your face, called the trigeminal nerve.
It sends out pain signals, but your brain feels them in your forehead instead.
The fix? Press your tongue to the roof of your mouth, to warm it back up.
